rv.q: And they are really bloody good, and watching them journey to the deepest recesses of the characters’ blurred souls is all you should want from the stage, really.
Yet, this intense, interval-free show is quite literally a game of two halves, Andrews’ overhaul of the ancient much more successful than his strangely sterile play on Bergman’s classic.
Andrews beautifully rethinks Sophocles but proves unequal to Bergman.

cn.t: Blanchett and Hoss's star power elevates this audacious but intellectually uneven mash-up of Sophocles' Electra and Bergman's Persona. The leads' coin-toss role swap adds meta-theatrical intrigue to Andrews' ambitious exploration of duality and identity.
